TechNicol Productions LLC is an Ohio-based technical services company, owned and operated by Lead Technician and Stagehand, Kevin Nicol.

We offer professional audio/visual engineering, live sound mixing, freelance stagehand labor, set and strike capabilities in all departments, RF frequency management, lighting execution, and versatile venue operations of all sorts.

We specialize in contract production services for corporate conferences, conventions, arena shows, and live entertainment venues.

Our mission is to deliver reliable, high-precision technical support, signal flow management, and stage operations for event planners, production agencies, and venues across the Greater Columbus area and beyond.

■ PART I — FOUR CHAPTERS OF GRIT, STAGECRAFT & FATHERHOOD

ACT I • BEFORE THE DECK (1981 – 2003) HONOLULU → OMAHA
Island Roots, Turning Pro on a Skateboard at 15, Self-Taught Sound & Call-Floor Grit

I was born and raised in Honolulu, Hawaii (Dec 1981), where I lived until I was eight with my parents, Brian and Colleen, and my younger brother, Daniel. After two years in Eugene, Oregon, my dad’s job brought us to Omaha, Nebraska in 1992—the big-town/small-city where I lived for 22 years, graduated from Omaha Central High School (Class of 2000), and cut my teeth.

Whenever something caught my fire, I taught myself how to take it to the next level. At age nine, I taught myself computer basics on an Apple IIe; while I’m no programmer, that early foundation gave me a solid, practical understanding of how computer hardware and software systems generally work. On the field and in the streets, it was first baseball—becoming one of the top Little League pitchers in town—and then skateboarding, where I turned professional at 15 years old. I served as Team Captain & Assistant Manager for Wise Guy Products Skate & Bike Team (1998–2003), Assistant Manager at Worldwize Skate Shop (2003), and Guest Pro Instructor at Lake Owen Skateboard Camp in Cable, Wisconsin (Summers 2001–2003). Taking hard slams on concrete built a physical grit and pain tolerance that later made 16-hour arena load-ins feel like second nature.

At the same time, I was completely self-taught on the guitar and keyboard, honing my ear for arrangements long before diving into digital audio workstation (DAW) production around 2004. I also learned how to talk to anyone under pressure—starting on dinner-hour cold calls for Bank of America / Dial America (1999–2000) and setting an all-time first-month new-hire sales record on a 200-seat call floor at Omaha Steaks (2002–2003), where management pulled me in without warning to teach the next training class of 30 reps how I did it. In 2003, I traded the call floor for live sets—taking my first PA and Grip calls with Oberon Entertainment, Douglas Productions / Steve Douglas Grip & Lighting, Actors Etc., Spirit Marketing, and Lee Tilford Advertising.

ACT II • ON THE ROAD & UNDER THE STAGE (2003 – 2015) 12 YRS FILM + 5 YRS UNION
Chvala & Company '3rd in Command', I.A.T.S.E. Local 42, T.M.S. Shop Prep & T.S.O.

For over 12 years (April 2003 – August 2015), I lived what I still call "the best job of my life so far" with Chvala & Company Productions in Omaha. On our tight, fast-moving documentary crew, Bill Chvala was Owner & Director, Bill’s brother Ron Chvala served as First Camera & Lighting Director, and I was '3rd in Command'—operating as Key Grip, Lead Location Audio Recordist / Boom Operator, Gaffer, and B-Camera Operator. Our work for Mosaic (documenting their 100-year history from Bethphage Mission), the Aurora Award-winning Boys Town Centennial, Omaha Area Catholic Schools, and Good Samaritan Hospitals caught the attention of The Opportunity Education Foundation (founded by Joe Ricketts). They contracted us as their exclusive global film crew—capturing and documenting curriculum lessons in Omaha classrooms and traveling for weeks at a time across Uganda, Tanzania, Zanzibar, the Congo, and Fiji (with Evangelism Explosion) to document solar water tanks, DVD/TV kits, and preloaded Wi-Fi tablets across 800+ Sister Schools. During this era, I also released my 12-track electronic album My Driving Silence (2006) and composed 6 original broadcast scores for the PBS documentary America’s Marine Aviators.

Whenever I wasn't on a plane or location shoot, I worked for 5 years with the I.A.T.S.E. Local 42 Stagehands Union (May 2008 – August 2013, Participant ID #422654) and Theatrical Media Services (T.M.S.), owned by Dave Matthews. In crews of 4 to 140+, I built and struck ~100 national arena tours—starting with my very first three concerts ever worked, which happened back-to-back in three straight days: Tom Petty on day one, followed immediately by Dave Matthews Band and Neil Diamond. Alongside those arena shows, I worked Broadway tours at the Omaha Orpheum Theatre, two Olympic-sized pools flown in from Italy for the 2008 & 2012 U.S. Olympic Swim Trials, and annual multi-week dual-coast arena tour rehearsals for Trans-Siberian Orchestra (T.S.O.) at Mid-America Center.

ACT III • THE FATHERHOOD PIVOT (2015 – 2024) WORK-FROM-HOME DAD
Walking Away from Two Dream Careers to Be Present for My Kids in Ohio

People sometimes look at my resume and ask why a guy who was flying to East Africa on a documentary film crew and building arena tours for Metallica and Billy Joel & Elton John suddenly pivoted to remote work in Ohio in 2015. The answer is simple: fatherhood.

When my firstborn son, Alex, moved with his mom to Northeast Ohio, I made the tough decision to give up the idea of being a long-distance dad living out of Pelican cases and off of tour buses and semi-trailers. In August 2015, I packed up my life in Omaha, resigned from Chvala & Company and the Local 42 stagehand circuit, and moved to Reynoldsburg / Greater Columbus, Ohio to be close to Alex—and later welcomed my younger children, Elle and Evin.

For nearly a decade, I intentionally traded the arena floor for a quiet basement home office so I could be a work-from-home father. And just like pitching, skateboarding, and stagecraft, I threw myself into remote communication and excelled: at Enterprise Holdings (2017–2018), I consistently ranked in the Top 100 monthly and hit #7 out of over 2,200 sales reps company-wide in June 2017; at Squaremouth / Tin Leg Travel Insurance (2019–2020), I earned my Ohio Resident Travel Insurance license and handled multi-channel brokerage calls and simultaneous live chats until the March 2020 COVID-19 travel shutdown; and at LiveOps (2022–2025), I ran 1099 remote customer support for major accounts including Nike Athletics while keeping my kids at the center of my schedule.

ACT IV • BACK ON THE STEEL (2025 – PRESENT) COLUMBUS, OHIO
Returning to Live Stagecraft in Central Ohio & Launching TechNicol Productions LLC

With my kids growing older, the pull of live production, heavy stage steel, and clean signal flow brought me right back to where I belong. In early 2025, I stepped back onto the Columbus venue deck with Rhino Staging (Feb–July 2025)—building the heavy steel stage frame for Tyler, The Creator’s CHROMAKOPIA World Tour at The Schottenstein Center, aligning regulation ice-rink plexiglass shielding outdoors at Ohio Stadium for the 2025 NHL Stadium Series (featuring Twenty One Pilots), and assembling springboard dance and competition cheer floors at the Greater Columbus Convention Center.

On July 23, 2026, I formally incorporated TechNicol Productions LLC (State of Ohio Entity #5651932—a play on my last name, Nicol), backed by active $1M/$2M Commercial General Liability Insurance, fresh OSHA 10 General Industry certification (#CS-0006366590), and American BLS CPR/AED & First Aid (#78022). Today, alongside contract calls with AKAV LLC (including a 3,000+ attendee medical convention at the GCCC in August 2026) and ON Services, I bring 15+ years of multi-department stagecraft (A2/L2/V2/B2)—uniting the relentless physical grit of a teen pro skateboarder, the global adaptability of a four-continent documentary film crew, the heavy-steel precision of ~100 union arena tours, and the calm, disciplined reliability forged during nearly a decade as a dedicated work-from-home father—to every single call in Central Ohio and beyond.
